question: A content moderation pipeline runs the same flagging prompt against a post three times and only removes the post if at least two of the three runs flag it as a violation. Which pattern is being used?
options: A) Routing, classifying the post first and directing it to the specialized moderation prompt for that content type
B) Parallelization by sectioning, splitting the moderation task into independent subtasks each handled by a separate specialized prompt
C) Orchestrator-workers, where a central LLM assigns each moderation pass to a different specialized worker prompt
D) Parallelization by voting, issuing multiple independent runs of the same prompt and aggregating the results by majority
correct_answers: D) Parallelization by voting, issuing multiple independent runs of the same prompt and aggregating the results by majority
explanations: Incorrect. Routing classifies input into one of several distinct paths; the scenario runs one prompt repeatedly rather than choosing among specialized prompts.
Incorrect. Sectioning splits a task into different independent subtasks; here the same prompt is repeated, not divided into distinct subtasks.
Incorrect. Orchestrator-workers dynamically assigns different subtasks to different workers; here the same subtask is repeated identically across all three runs.
Correct. Running the identical prompt multiple times and aggregating results by a majority threshold is the defining shape of parallelization by voting.
